Confidence intervals for dependability and SEM in D-Study plans

Source: R/api-multivariate-dstudy-intervals.R, R/api-multivariate-dstudy-summary.R, R/api-plotting-dstudy-intervals.R
confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study.Rd

Quantify source-G-Study sampling uncertainty in relative G, absolute dependability Phi, or measurement SEM for prespecified future facet counts. Future counts do not add source degrees of freedom. Inspect Estimate/PointStatus separately from Lower/Upper/Status (an unavailable negative-variance point can coexist with a valid interval, and NA bounds never denote zero uncertainty).

Read G, Phi and measurement SEM together with their confidence intervals, methods and limitations. Ordinary summary(d) retains its coefficient-table return value. Request intervals explicitly, or reuse saved interval results.

Compare future plans on one shared coefficient or SEM axis. Each plan has adjacent method rows, distinguished by color, point shape and line type. Method agreement in a single dataset is not evidence of coverage.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_multivariate_d_study'
confint(
  object,
  parm = "G",
  level = 0.95,
  score = NULL,
  composite = NULL,
  assumption,
  draws = 100000L,
  seed = 1L,
  reference = NULL,
  method = "auto",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_multivariate_d_study'
summary(
  object,
  intervals = FALSE,
  parm = c("G", "Phi", "RelativeSEM", "AbsoluteSEM"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study'
print(x, digits = NULL, row.names = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_dstudy_intervals'
plot(
  x,
  draw = TRUE,
  preset = "standard",
  ncol = 2L,
  layout = c("combined", "panels"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A result from mfrm_d_study().

parm

Metrics to calculate when intervals = TRUE. The default includes "G", "Phi", "RelativeSEM" and "AbsoluteSEM". Select fewer metrics when only those answer your question, particularly for explicitly requested expensive profile methods.

level

Pointwise confidence level in (0, 1).

score

Select either one original score name or one named composite ("Composite" for vector weights; defaults to the sole composite or first original score).

composite

Select either one original score name or one named composite ("Composite" for vector weights; defaults to the sole composite or first original score).

assumption

Required "normal", asserting independent normal random Person, facet, interaction, and residual effects with constant variances.

draws

Pivotal draw count (>= 1000, >= 100 expected per tail; default 100000) and nonnegative integer seed (1 default; caller RNG restored) for one-facet Phi GCI; unused by other methods.

seed

Pivotal draw count (>= 1000, >= 100 expected per tail; default 100000) and nonnegative integer seed (1 default; caller RNG restored) for one-facet Phi GCI; unused by other methods.

reference

Optional row index in object$design_grid returning each other plan minus the reference plan (NULL returns individual plans).

method

"auto" (default: "exact_f" for one-facet G, "gci" for one-facet Phi and unchanged-child nested reduction, "mls" for balanced two-crossed-facet G/Phi and SEM), or an explicit choice / compatible comparison vector from:

  • "mls": quadratic Ting (1990) null inversion h(rho)'lambda = 0 for balanced two-crossed-facet G/Phi (FormulaComplete = FALSE flags conservatively retained negative-squared-width ranges), or Graybill-Wang / Ting error-variance intervals square-rooted for SEM.

  • "approximate_f": Satterthwaite F inversion (1 - rho)*MS_P / D(rho) for crossed (Wong & McGraw, 1999) or general nested G/Phi (using expected-mean-square coefficients with m = r/R, h = t/T).

  • "mean_square_region": conservative Charnes-Cooper LP projection over the level^(1/J) joint chi-square mean-square region intersected with theta >= 0 (lpSolve required; supports individual plans and shared-region reference enclosures).

  • "score": experimental extended-nuisance score inversion T = kappa^2 sum_j 2 h_j^2 lambda_j^2 / df_j <= qchisq(level, 1) for balanced two-crossed-facet G (Empty = TRUE vs NumericalComplete).

  • "reml_profile": experimental normal REML deviance inversion (D - D_min <= qchisq(level, 1), lme4/minqa, plus nloptr for direct multi-count differences) on retained ratings (IntervalCenter records the separate REML center; CandidateLower/Upper retain exploratory bounds on numerical failure).

  • "spectral_f": exact normal-model F pivot F(t) = {sum(z_i^2 / (1 + lambda_i*t)) / r} / (S_E / nu) (E, Hannig, & Iyer, 2008) after projecting off facet incidence for incomplete/balanced one-facet G and reference differences.

  • "residual_contrast": exact normal-residual chi-square projection mapped by sigma_E / sqrt(m) for one-facet RelativeSEM and reference differences on balanced or incomplete ratings (IntervalCenter separate).

  • "delta": first-order sampling SE \(\sqrt{g^\top \hat C g}\) and unclipped normal limits Estimate +/- z * SE for individual-plan G/Phi using \(\hat C\) from vcov.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy() (Almehrizi, 2021; OutsideParameterSpace and AtBoundary flag boundary limits).

...

Reserved; additional arguments are rejected.

intervals

FALSE (default) returns the original coefficient table. TRUE calculates the selected intervals using confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study(). Alternatively supply a saved confint(d) result or a list of such results. Saved results may contain different metrics, methods, scores or reference plans, but must match this D-study's source, plans and score weights. GENOVA-adjusted results retain adjusted points alongside original-source population intervals, with separate IntervalEstimate and IntervalBasis. Saved intervals must match the component treatment too.

x

A result from confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study().

digits

Display precision passed to the printed tables; NULL uses R's current setting. Stored estimates are unchanged.

row.names

Logical; print table row names? Defaults to FALSE.

draw

Logical; FALSE returns the plot data without opening a device.

preset

Package plot style, including "standard" (color) and "monochrome". Methods also have distinct point shapes.

ncol

Positive integer number of columns for layout = "panels". Unused by the default combined view.

layout

"combined" (default) groups methods within each plan on one axis, with a common method legend. "panels" retains one panel per future plan, with at most ncol columns.

Value

A data.frame of class mfrm_dstudy_intervals containing plan counts, Kind, Score, Metric, Estimate, PointStatus, Lower, Upper, RawRatioLower/RawRatioUpper (balanced F/GCI), Level, Method, Status, MethodCode, Available, NegativeComponent, and Validation, plus method-specific columns (SE, SamplingVariance, SEStatus, AtBoundary, OutsideParameterSpace for "delta"; FormulaComplete, NumericalComplete, Empty for "mls"/"score"; IntervalCenter, CandidateLower/Upper for "reml_profile" / "residual_contrast"; ErrorVariance, ErrorVarianceSE, RawVarianceLower/Upper for MLS SEM; Reference* for reference contrasts) and portable attributes (diagnostics, pivot, monte_carlo, source_summary, nesting_context, notes).

With intervals = FALSE, the unchanged object$coefficients data frame. Otherwise a summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study list containing:

  • table: one row per returned plan, metric and method, with Interval identifying the entry in intervals. It retains all original interval columns, including point/interval status, qualifications and any separate REML or residual-contrast IntervalCenter. Columns not applicable to a method are NA.

  • intervals: the complete original interval objects, retaining notes, diagnostics, reference context and their existing plot() methods.

  • source_design, source_rows, design_grid, weights and component_diagnostics: the original design, score and review context.

  • notes: method qualifications and interpretation reminders. print() returns the same saved summary invisibly. For G/Phi with method = "delta", the table retains and prints the coefficient sampling SE, distinct from measurement SEM. For GENOVA-adjusted points it is named IntervalSE and describes the original estimator, not the adjusted point. Normal-reference bounds outside [0,1] are not clipped.

Invisibly, a ggplot object; plot_data() retains the exact table, unavailable rows, source intervals, design_grid, weights and notes. as_ggplot() remains idempotent on the returned object. No title or explanatory footnote is drawn.

Details

One-facet pivots and plan differences. For observed facet count k, future count m, and R = 1 + k * sigma_P^2 / sigma_E^2, "exact_f" intersects (MS_P / MS_E) / F_quantiles with R >= 1 before mapping G_m = m*(R - 1) / (m*(R - 1) + k) (Status = "Empty parameter-space interval" if wholly below 1). One-facet "gci" draws Q_j = df_j * MS_j / X_j and evaluates Mondal et al. (2025, Eq. 11) max(0, Q_P - Q_E) / (Q_P + (k/n)*Q_F + (k - 1 - k/n)*Q_E), mapping to Phi_m = m*rho / (1 + (m - 1)*rho) (attr(ci, "monte_carlo") stores binomial order-statistic endpoint bands). With reference (a vs b), shared-ratio methods map the entire base interval for t through h(t) = (b - a)*t / ((1 + a*t)*(1 + b*t)), including the interior stationary point t = 1 / sqrt(a*b), rather than subtracting marginal endpoints.

Nested reduction and GENOVA adjustments. When raters are nested within tasks and future child counts per parent match the balanced source count R, cell means reduce G/Phi to the one-facet sampling law over parent counts; changed child counts require explicit "approximate_f", "mean_square_region", "reml_profile", or "delta". For GENOVA-adjusted D-Studies, Estimate retains the adjusted point while IntervalEstimate and bounds target the unadjusted population parameter (ComponentTreatment, IntervalBasis); finite-sample interval behavior depends on source degrees of freedom and rating-plan balance.

The intervals describe uncertainty from the observed G-study in the population coefficient or SEM of a specified future complete plan. They do not represent data already collected under that future plan. G and Phi are dimensionless; SEM is in the selected score's units. A larger G/Phi or smaller SEM does not alone determine a worthwhile plan: consider the intended decision, score meaning and task/rater burden.

reference requests the selected method's shared-source plan differences for each metric; this is not subtraction of independently constructed marginal intervals. For a balanced two-facet source, explicitly select method = "mean_square_region" for conservative joint-region enclosures. This summary is not an input to recommend_mfrm_design(), whose D-study route uses mfrm_d_study_comparison. Positive G/Phi differences and negative SEM differences favor the comparison plan, conditional on the stated model. Individual-plan and difference results remain explicitly labeled if both are supplied as saved results.

Printing and reopening a saved summary do not calculate intervals or refit models. Printing separates the main estimates, method qualifications and rows with unavailable points/intervals or incomplete width formulas; table retains all statuses and diagnostics columns. A completed approximate interval is qualified by its method, not automatically labeled a failure. Save the complete summary with saveRDS() to retain its context; CSV export of table alone loses weights, notes and diagnostics. Use plot(s$intervals[[1]]) for its existing forest plot, or supply a suitable single-metric individual-plan result to plot(d, intervals = ...). A summary does not create simultaneous guarantees across metrics, scores or selected plans. Read each method's qualifications. Availability is not proof of model validity or accurate finite-sample coverage.

All methods concern the same score/composite, metric and source data. A filled point has an interval; an open point is an available estimate without an interval. Unavailable intervals are explicitly labeled in the combined view, or marked by an asterisk in the panel view, even if their point estimates are missing. An interval can exist without an admissible ANOVA/MINQUE point estimate. Missing values remain missing; no substitute interval or zero is drawn. The shared axis includes [0,1] for coefficients and [-1,1] for G/Phi differences, expanding to retain all finite estimates and accepted bounds. Delta normal-reference bounds outside [0,1] remain visible; they flag limitations of that approximation, not a larger population parameter space. SEM and SEM-difference axes instead span the estimates and intervals in score units, including zero. Negative SEM differences favor the comparison plan. An SEM interval is uncertainty in measurement error, not an interval for a Person's score. Chi-square and MLS labels retain the calculation used for each plan; their assumptions and coverage claims differ. Method limitations, confidence level, normal-effect assumptions and negative components remain in the returned notes and source object. Plotting neither refits a model nor recalculates an interval. Save the complete interval or plot object with saveRDS() for later use. Nested plan labels show child counts per parent, rather than total child pool sizes; the reference plan uses the same count convention. A mean-square-region difference is a conservative enclosure from shared source uncertainty, not a tight joint image or a paired-delta interval. Its returned source retains the individual projections and reference. REML profile and residual-contrast rows retain the original source points; the separate IntervalCenter and method diagnostics are available in the source interval object. A point can lie outside this separately calculated interval. For GENOVA-adjusted results, points use the selected component treatment; intervals retain their original-source population basis. IntervalEstimate and IntervalBasis in the source table distinguish them. Drawing the two together does not make the original sampling SE an adjusted-estimator SE. Unresolved numerical candidates are retained in the source object but are not drawn as accepted confidence bounds. For exact-F, score and MLS intervals, an empty confidence set is labeled "Empty set"; it is distinct from an estimated coefficient of zero. MLS rows with FormulaComplete = FALSE retain candidate values where a squared width is undefined. Their conservative bounds are drawn, while the saved interval object and notes retain the reason and affected ranges.

Choose the operation

print(d) displays the D-study and returns it invisibly; summary(d) returns its coefficient table. This opt-in summary collects intervals; confint(d) calculates one metric at a time with the same inference rules. Neither changes d. print(s) displays the saved summary without any estimation, and s$table is the data frame for subsetting or CSV export. Use plot(d) for planning curves and plot(s$intervals$Phi) for a saved interval forest. A summary list itself is not a new plotting input.

This page explains the interface and reading order. Mathematical constructions, design-specific assumptions, numerical diagnostics and references are in confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study().

Session plot defaults

See mfrmr_visual_diagnostics for options(mfrmr.plot_preset), argument precedence, and appearance when saving or reusing a plot.

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tasks <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mgenova-table12.csv", package = "mfrmr"))
g <- mfrm_g_study(tasks, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL)
d <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)),
  weights = c(V = .5, W = .5))
ci <- confint(d, assumption = "normal")
ci[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
attr(ci, "notes")
# Optional normal approximation: SE describes the coefficient, not measurement SEM.
delta_ci <- confint(d, method = "delta", assumption = "normal")
delta_ci[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "SE", "Lower", "Upper", "SEStatus")]
phi_ci <- confint(d, parm = "Phi", assumption = "normal", seed = 1)
phi_ci[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
attr(phi_ci, "monte_carlo")$endpoint_bands
# How much would G improve by changing from six to twelve tasks?
change <- confint(d, parm = "G", reference = 1, assumption = "normal")
change[, c("Tasks", "ReferenceCount", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
# The same planning question for absolute dependability; coverage is approximate.
phi_change <- confint(d, parm = "Phi", reference = 1, assumption = "normal")
phi_change[, c("Tasks", "ReferenceCount", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
attr(phi_change, "monte_carlo")$endpoint_bands
# Sampling uncertainty in measurement SEM, rather than in G or Phi.
sem_ci <- confint(d, parm = "AbsoluteSEM", assumption = "normal")
sem_ci[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Method", "Status")]
sem_change <- confint(d, parm = "RelativeSEM", reference = 1,
                      assumption = "normal")
sem_change[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
sem_plot <- plot(d, type = "sem", metric = "AbsoluteSEM", intervals = TRUE,
                 assumption = "normal", draw = FALSE)
plot_data(sem_plot, "notes")
# Different raters serve each task; retain three raters per task.
data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_nested", package = "mfrmr")
gn <- mfrm_g_study(mfrmr_example_gtheory_nested,
  c("Content", "Organization"), nesting = c(Rater = "Task"))
dn <- mfrm_d_study(gn,
  data.frame(Raters = 3, Tasks = c(6, 12)))
nested_change <- confint(dn, parm = "G", reference = 1, assumption = "normal")
nested_change[, c("Raters", "Tasks", "ReferenceCount", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper")]
attr(nested_change, "nesting_context")
# Incomplete one-facet ratings: relative SEM without likelihood fitting.
observed <- tasks[(tasks$Person + tasks$Task) %% 3 != 0, ]
sparse_g <- mfrm_g_study(observed, "V", rater = NULL, method = "minque0")
sparse_d <- mfrm_d_study(sparse_g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)))
residual_sem <- confint(sparse_d, parm = "RelativeSEM",
  method = "residual_contrast", assumption = "normal")
residual_sem[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
residual_change <- confint(sparse_d, parm = "RelativeSEM", reference = 1,
  method = "residual_contrast", assumption = "normal")
residual_change[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper")]
# Relative G also uses Person variation; normal Person effects are required.
spectral_g <- confint(sparse_d, method = "spectral_f", assumption = "normal")
spectral_g[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
spectral_change <- confint(sparse_d, method = "spectral_f", reference = 1,
  assumption = "normal")
spectral_change[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper")]
# A separate experimental REML model can address G/Phi or absolute SEM.
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("minqa", quietly = TRUE)) {
  profile_ci <- confint(sparse_d, method = "reml_profile", assumption = "normal")
  profile_ci[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper", "Validation")]
  attr(profile_ci, "notes")
  # Uncertainty in absolute measurement SEM, in score units.
  profile_sem <- confint(sparse_d, parm = "AbsoluteSEM",
                         method = "reml_profile", assumption = "normal")
  plot(sparse_d, type = "sem", metric = "AbsoluteSEM", intervals = profile_sem,
       draw = FALSE)
  # How much does doubling the task count change G?
  profile_change <- confint(sparse_d, reference = 1,
    method = "reml_profile", assumption = "normal")
  profile_change[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper")]
  attr(profile_change, "base_interval")
  plot(profile_change, draw = FALSE)
}
# Start with the default two-crossed-facet approximation on bundled data.
data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed", package = "mfrmr")
crossed <- mfrm_g_study(mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed,
  c("Content", "Organization"))
future <- mfrm_d_study(crossed,
  data.frame(Raters = c(2, 4), Tasks = c(6, 12)),
  weights = c(Content = .5, Organization = .5))
crossed_ci <- confint(future, parm = "Phi", assumption = "normal")
crossed_ci[, c("Raters", "Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper",
               "FormulaComplete", "Status")]
attr(crossed_ci, "notes")
# The score method remains an explicit experimental comparison for G.
score_ci <- confint(future, method = "score", assumption = "normal")
score_ci[, c("Scenario", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Empty", "Status")]
# Vary task counts within each rater count to obtain planning-curve ribbons.
curve_plans <- mfrm_d_study(crossed,
  expand.grid(Raters = c(2, 4), Tasks = c(3, 6, 12)),
  weights = c(Content = .5, Organization = .5))
score_curve <- plot(curve_plans, metric = "G", intervals = TRUE,
  method = "score", assumption = "normal", draw = FALSE)
plot_data(score_curve, "notes")
if (requireNamespace("lpSolve", quietly = TRUE)) {
  comparison <- confint(future, parm = "Phi", assumption = "normal",
    method = c("mls", "approximate_f", "mean_square_region"))
  comparison[, c("Scenario", "Method", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
  figure <- plot(comparison, draw = FALSE)
  plot_data(figure, "notes")
  if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) as_ggplot(figure)
  # General nested comparison: both counts change, with eighteen ratings.
  general_nested <- mfrm_d_study(gn,
    data.frame(Raters = c(3, 2, 6), Tasks = c(6, 9, 3)))
  nested_region <- confint(general_nested, parm = "Phi", reference = 1,
    method = "mean_square_region", assumption = "normal")
  nested_region[, c("Raters", "Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
  attr(nested_region, "reference")$counts
}
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Published synthetic data, not empirical speech-contest records.
ratings <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mgenova-table12.csv", package = "mfrmr"))
g <- mfrm_g_study(ratings, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL)
d <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)),
  weights = c(V = .5, W = .5))
# Compare dependability and measurement error under the normal-effects model.
s <- summary(d, intervals = TRUE, assumption = "normal")
print(s, digits = 3)
# One row per plan for absolute dependability; the complete table is retained.
subset(s$table, Metric == "Phi",
  select = c(Tasks, Estimate, Lower, Upper, Status))
# Reuse an interval for a curve, with no interval calculation.
p <- plot(d, metric = "Phi", intervals = s$intervals$Phi, draw = FALSE)
plot_data(p, "notes")
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("plot.mfrm_dstudy_intervals", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tasks <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mgenova-table12.csv", package = "mfrmr"))
g <- mfrm_g_study(tasks, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL)
d <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)))
ci <- confint(d, assumption = "normal")
p <- plot(ci, draw = FALSE)
plot_data(p, "notes")
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) as_ggplot(p)
} # }
